ai.title: Terminal command detection threshold lowered to 3 words
ai.summary: Reduced word count limit for automatic terminal command detection from 5 to 3 in npm-app/src/cli.ts. This change aims to reduce false positives where natural language inputs are incorrectly parsed as commands. The logic still respects SKIPPED_TERMINAL_COMMANDS and the 'run' prefix.

eli5.text: The tool now treats any phrase you type with three or fewer words as a possible command instead of waiting for five or fewer. This means shorter phrases are more likely to be run as commands, and the system still avoids running certain built-in phrases and ones that start with 'run'. You would notice the assistant reacting to shorter inputs as if they were commands, even when you meant to speak normally.

ai.title: System prompt: remove git operations, add git commit/rebase guardrail
ai.summary: Removes 'Performing git operations' from the allowed `run_terminal_command` use cases in `backend/src/system-prompt.ts`. Adds explicit constraint: 'Don't run git commit or git rebase or related commands unless you get explicit permission from the user.' Fixes duplicate numbering in guidelines list.

eli5.text: Starting today, the assistant you interact with will no longer run certain version-control commands on its own (like automatically creating code snapshots or moving code between drafts). These actions now require your direct approval before they happen. If you were used to seeing automatic commits or rebases during collaborative coding sessions, those will no longer occur without you explicitly asking for them.

ai.title: Add add and hey to skipped terminal commands
ai.summary: Added 'add' and 'hey' to SKIPPED_TERMINAL_COMMANDS in common/src/constants.ts. Updated CLI logic in npm-app/src/cli.ts to bypass command parsing if input contains 'error '. This prevents specific short inputs from being incorrectly processed as terminal commands.

eli5.text: The assistant will no longer treat the simple inputs "add" and "hey" as commands to run in a terminal. If a message contains the word "error " (with a space), command parsing is also skipped. This affects anyone typing short phrases that could otherwise be mistaken for terminal commands, and it is already live.

ai.title: Include shell config files in project context
ai.summary: Adds user shell configuration files to the AI context window. `common/src/util/file.ts` extends `ProjectFileContextSchema` with `shellConfigFiles`. `npm-app/src/project-files.ts` implements `loadShellConfigFiles` to read standard dotfiles (`.bashrc`, `.zshrc`, etc.) from the home directory, filtering missing files. `backend/src/system-prompt.ts` injects these contents into the prompt via a new `<user_shell_config_files>` block.

eli5.text: When you start a chat with the assistant, it can now read your personal command-line customization files (like.bashrc or.zshrc) that live in your home folder and include snippets from them in what it sees. This means the assistant gains visibility into any environment variables, aliases, or functions you've set up for your shell. The change is already active in the backend code, so anyone using the tool with existing shell config files will have those files pulled into the context automatically; you'd notice this only if you happened to spot your own dotfiles content appearing in the prompt the assistant builds.

ai.title: Version 1.0.78
ai.summary: Version bump to 1.0.78 in npm-app/package.json. No functional code changes.

eli5.text: The Home page no longer shows an email signup form with a submit button. Instead, visitors see a link that takes them directly to the Manicode npm page. If you open the website today, you won't find a field to type your email anymore. The old signup input and its button have been removed entirely.
